newsitem.title: GERMANY: VW unveils fourth generation of Golf.
newsitem.headline: VW unveils fourth generation of Golf.

text.p: Volkswagen AG unveiled the fourth generation of the world's best-selling Golf model Tuesday, and sources at the German automaker said VW has an ambitious goal of selling 2 million of the vehicles a year.

VW expects explosive demand for the new model, which was shown to the media for the first time in Bonn, and believe it can meet customer demand without adding new plants or boosting its full-time work force, the sources told Reuters.

In addition, VW officials say they will aggressively price the new Golf against chief European market competitors such as General Motor Corp.'s new Opel Astra model, due to go on sale next April, and the Escort from Ford Motor Co.

The new Golf, which usually commands a premium, was priced at 25,700 marks, ($13,980) about 400 marks ($220) cheaper than a comparable model despite a series of new standard equipment. "The market analysis shows excellent demand for the new Golf," one VW source said. He declined to be more specific as to how long it will take VW to ramp up Golf production toward 2 million vehicles from the 1996 level of about 700,000.

VW Chief Executive Ferdinand Piech said in a television interview late Monday that VW expects to sell at least 700,000 of the new Golf models in Europe alone in the first year after the car goes on sale in October.

"It is without a doubt the bread from which we live," said VW spokesman Klaus Kocks, noting that the Golf accounts for half of the Volkswagen brand's output and a fifth of all cars sold within the company, whose makes include Audi, SEAT and Skoda.
VW investors are cheering the new model, seen as one reason for VW stock more than doubling in price so far this year.

"Should sales be successful, then we expect clearly more gains in VW shares," said ABN Amro Bank in a report, noting VW shares could climb to 2,300 marks in the next 12 to 18 months from the current level of about 1,350 marks.
Volkswagen has put much effort into designing the new Golf, which originally made its debut in March 1974. It has been the backbone of VW's sales, and nearly 18 million have now been produced.

While the new Golf shows a lot of family resemblance, the car has been revamped with bolder styling lines to make it longer and roomier than the current model as well as to make important improvements in safety, such as side air bags.
"It's what customers want," Piech said in the television interview, commenting on the likeness to old Golf models. But he quickly added, "It's a totally new car from top to bottom."
The new Golf will face a tough market in the compact class, in part due to the launch by Mercedes-Benz of the A-class subcompact and new model offerings from Opel and Ford.
"I think VW will have to go beyond their normal market for the Golf and try to extend the reach with the new one," said Jonathan Storey at European Automotive Research in Britain.
